contentBlocks.text: Last week you explored forces and motion. This week: a new topic, life cycles — the stages every living thing goes through!

A life cycle is the series of stages a living thing goes through as it's born, grows, and eventually reproduces to make new offspring. A butterfly's life cycle has 4 clear stages: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa (chrysalis), and adult butterfly. Put these 4 stages in the correct order, and explain what happens at each one in your own words.
You just learned what a life cycle is, using a butterfly's dramatic transformation! Tomorrow we'll compare it to a very different kind of life cycle.

objectives: Define a life cycle as the stages an organism goes through from birth to reproduction
Correctly sequence the butterfly's 4 life-cycle stages: egg, larva, pupa, adult
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's forces-and-motion work briefly.
2. Introduce the life-cycle concept using the butterfly's 4 stages.
3. Have the child sequence and describe each stage.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's comparison to a different life cycle.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use pictures or drawings of each stage as physical cards to sequence, rather than sequencing from memory alone
Ready for more: ask the child what they think would happen if the pupa stage were skipped
The butterfly's dramatic visible transformation makes it the strongest opening example for this concept
teacherGuide.answerKey: The correct order is: egg, larva (caterpillar), pupa (chrysalis), adult butterfly.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 3 Life Science standard 3-LS1-1: developing models to describe an organism's unique and generalized life cycles, opening this week's life-cycles thread from the course's own description.
